<strong>C’est un dimanche après-midi. No: It is a Sunday afternoon, September 21, 2025. Nooran and five of his friends are sitting on the sidewalk in front of a house in Saint-Hubert when SPAL officers respond to a 911 call. In less than 10 seconds, shots are fired and the teenager is shot dead.
<strong>Six mois plus tard, les cinq jeu: Six months later, the five youths, still marked by the events, are suing the City of Longueuil and its police service for nearly $1.9M, with the support of their mothers. What does this lawsuit reveal about the Nooran case? And about the system’s ability to establish accountability?
Échecs scolaires et expulsions, détresse: Academic failure and expulsions, psychological distress, behavioural problems, strained relationships with family members: the lawyers paint a worrying portrait of the situation of five youths and of the current or potential repercussions of the tragedy on them.
L’intervention policière qui a coûté la: The police intervention that cost 15-year-old Nooran Rezayi his life allegedly caused significant lasting harm to the five teenagers who were at the scene of the tragedy. That is what the lawyers representing these youths and their families will try to prove. A civil suit was filed in Quebec Superior Court on March 19. It targets the City of Longueuil and two officers of its police service who were involved in the deadly intervention.
« Ils ne vont pas très bien. L’événement: “They’re not doing very well. The event is very recent – it’s been six months. It’s very likely that they have post-traumatic shock. It takes time to appear…” M<sup>e</sup> Virginie Dufresne-Lemire, one of the lawyers representing the plaintiffs, tells us.
« Leur ami est mort devant eux de manièr: “Their friend died in front of them in a completely – in our view – unjustified way,” says the lawyer, who specializes in defending victims of police abuse. “There is a lot of incomprehension, anger; a loss of trust in government institutions. (…) Their path is incredibly affected. Their world is collapsing. These are lives that have been turned upside down.”
On se souviendra que, dans les moments q: It will be remembered that in the moments before the police intervention in the residential neighbourhood of Saint-Hubert, Nooran was with five other youths. After a 911 call, police officers arrived on the scene. One of them ordered the youths to lie on the ground. A few seconds later, Nooran was shot. Resuscitation efforts were then attempted, in vain. He was pronounced dead at the hospital. According to <l1>an article</l1> from Radio-Canada, five minutes passed between the gunshots and the start of efforts to try to save the wounded teenager.
« Entre le moment où le véhicule s’immob: “Less than 10 seconds pass between the moment the vehicle comes to a stop and the shots. Less than 3 seconds pass between the moment the first order is shouted and the shots,” the authors of the lawsuit note in the court documents. They explain that the action is aimed “particularly at the highly negligent and reckless actions of two SPAL (Service de police de l’agglomération de Longueuil) officers.”
Ce délai entre le premier ordre et les c: That delay between the first order and the gunshots is extremely short, M<sup>e</sup> Dufresne-Lemire insists. “The judge will ask: ‘Would a reasonable police officer, placed in the same circumstances, have fired?’” she continues. It will have to be determined whether there was imminent danger.
Aucune arme à feu n’a été retrouvée sur: No firearm was found on the youths. Only a baseball bat.
Pour les adolescents qui ont été témoins: According to their lawyers, the teenagers who witnessed the intervention suffered “heavy damages.” The youths, all minors, are not identified in the court documents for the moment. However, the documents include an account of the consequences of the tragedy on their daily lives and, by extension, on those of members of their immediate families.
Il y a le cas de deux jumeaux de 15 ans,: There is the case of two 15-year-old twins who are related to Nooran. On that fateful day, they watched their best friend die before their eyes. Both feared they would also be targeted by the officers’ gunfire during the intervention. The situation is described as traumatic. Sadness, anger, lack of motivation and a sense of injustice have weighed on them since the events. The twins, who were in their 4<sup>th</sup> year of high school, saw their grades drop after the tragedy. They also have behavioural problems, particularly toward authority figures. Both ended up being expelled from their school.
La relation avec leur mère est également: Their relationship with their mother is also affected, since she asks them not to go out, fearing for their safety, which causes friction. “Before the intervention, she had never had a bad experience with the police, for whom she felt only consideration and respect. But since Nooran’s death, she has lost all trust in them and instead sees them as a threat to her sons’ safety,” reads the lawsuit document.
Cette méfiance envers la police est auss: This distrust of the police is also mentioned several times among the youths. One of them fears the police and is frightened by the sound of patrol car sirens that accompanies the flashing lights. At night, “he has nightmares in which the police show up at his home and kill him.” Also 15 years old, “he no longer has any motivation at school, even though he has always cared about doing well.” Sports activities he used to enjoy interest him less and he is isolating himself socially.
L’indemnisation réclamée avoisine les 1,: The compensation sought is close to $1.9M. Part of that sum would make it possible to provide, among other things, psychological or therapeutic care for five youths and four adults. The rest, an amount of $1M, represents punitive damages, intended to penalize reprehensible conduct and deter such behaviour from happening again.
Selon les poursuivants, une série d’erre: According to the plaintiffs, a series of errors were allegedly made, such as poor planning of the intervention, insufficient de-escalation measures, or the use of a firearm without legitimate justification, for example.
L’habillement même de la victime ne corr: Even the victim’s clothing did not match what was mentioned in the 911 call. The call reported an individual wearing black pants; Nooran was wearing white shorts.
« Les policiers ont mis en danger l’ense: “The officers endangered all of the youths and the surrounding citizens, including children, in addition to making an abusive and disproportionate use of force,” allege the authors of the lawsuit.
De surcroît, ils soutiennent que le prof: Moreover, they argue that racial profiling may have been a factor explaining the speed with which lethal force was used. “We’re talking about an intervention that escalates extremely quickly, we’re talking about six racialized youths and a history of profiling problems within the SPAL: in our view, these are indicators of racial profiling,” says M<sup>e</sup> Dufresne-Lemire.
Parmi les fautes alléguées, on note auss: Among the alleged faults is also the disclosure of confidential information to the media. According to the plaintiffs, SPAL officers allegedly passed the content of the 911 call to a journalist. “This unusual leak of information had the sole purpose of influencing public opinion and justifying the officer’s use of his service weapon during the intervention,” they contend.
Contactée par La Converse, la Ville de L: Contacted by La Converse, the City of Longueuil responded in a written statement that it will not comment on the matter because it is before the courts.
En plus de réclamer une compensation fin: In addition to seeking financial compensation to provide adequate psychological support to the teenagers and their mothers, the plaintiffs hope to obtain answers about what happened. They also want greater accountability from the City of Longueuil, as well as from its police officers, even though the latter do a job that can be dangerous.
Pour le moment, plusieurs zones d’ombre: For now, several grey areas remain in the account of the events that led to Nooran’s death. The content of the report by the Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes (BEI) is not public. The families want a complete picture of the situation. Filing a civil suit could allow them to obtain clarification. Among that clarification would be the BEI report.
Ultimement, la question qui se pose est: Ultimately, the question is: “How do we prevent such a tragedy from happening again?” sums up M<sup>e</sup> Dufresne-Lemire. “These mothers are afraid, it could have been their son,” she says, reporting that some now suffer from anxiety and insomnia.
La réponse à cette question, l’avocate a: The lawyer admits she does not yet have the answer to that question. She strongly hopes the legal process can help achieve some progress. Deaths during police interventions are not a new phenomenon. “Why does this still continue today? It’s a really complex question. We can certainly reflect on police culture, on the impunity that reigns,” the lawyer suggests.
La formation est souvent présentée comme: Training is often presented as part of the solution, but it has its limits, she says. “There are requirements to take training in order to be qualified to use a firearm, but there is no annual requirement when it comes to de-escalation,” she illustrates.
Mentionnons que le <l1>rapport du corone: It should be noted that the <l1>coroner’s report</l1> on the death of Pierre Coriolan, shot by the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM) in 2017, recommended, among other things, making annual requalification in de-escalation and tactical communication mandatory for police officers.
« Une arme à feu, c’est mortel, on ne re: “A firearm is deadly, there’s no going back: we need to think about the power police officers have to use force,” says M<sup>e</sup> Dufresne-Lemire.

If the case proceeds through the courts, obtaining a judgment could take three to seven years, according to the lawyer.
